'''''Crassula helmsii''''', known as '''swamp stonecrop''' or '''New Zealand pigmyweed''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is an [[aquatic plant|aquatic]] or semiterrestrial species of [[succulent plant]] in the family [[Crassulaceae]].<ref name="Invade">{{cite web |url=http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=1517&fr=1&sts=&lang=EN |title=''Crassula helmsii'' (aquatic plant, succulent) |date=April 15, 2010 |work=Global Invasive Species Database |publisher=ISSG |access-date=March 8, 2012 |archive-date=May 9, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120509205223/http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=1517&fr=1&sts=&lang=EN |url-status=dead }}</ref> Originally found in Australia and New Zealand, it has been introduced around the world. In the United Kingdom, this plant is one of five introduced [[Invasive species|invasive]] aquatic plants that were banned from sale from April 2014, the first ban of its kind in the country.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-21232108|title = UK bans sale of five invasive non-native aquatic plants|work = BBC News|date = 29 January 2013}}</ref> It is on the [[Global Biodiversity Information Facility]]'s [[Global Register of Introduced and Invasive Species]] of eleven countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/8035075|title=Crassula helmsii A.Berger|website=www.gbif.org|language=en|access-date=2020-04-04}}</ref>

==Description==
The shoots are rather stiff, carrying narrow parallel-sided [[Leaf|leaves]] in opposite pairs, each leaf being about {{convert|4|-|24|mm}}. Small white [[Flower|flowers]] with four petals are produced in summer on long stalks arising from the upper leaf axils. The flowers are always above water.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}

==Distribution==
{{Expand section|date=April 2022}}
''C. helmsii'' was recorded in 2010 throughout the British Isles, in the Netherlands, Belgium, the United States, Russia, France, Germany, Italy and Spain<ref name="Invade"/>
In Ireland, ''C. helmsii'' has been recorded on waste ground in Ireland at [[Howth Head]], County Dublin,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ni Dhuill |first=E. |date=2021 |title=Invasive non-native and alien garden escape plant species on the southern cliffs of Howth Head, Co. Dublin (H21) |journal=Irish Naturalists' Journal |volume=37 |number=2 |pages=102–108}}</ref> and at a number of sites in Northern Ireland.<ref name="hackney">{{cite web |url=http://www.habitas.org.uk/invasive/species.asp?item=4639 |title=Crassula helmsii, New Zealand Pigmyweed |first=Paul |last=Hackney |date=n.d. |website=Invasive Alien Species in Northern Ireland |publisher=National Museums Northern Ireland |access-date=17 April 2022 |archive-date=20 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420132703/http://www.habitas.org.uk/invasive/species.asp?item=4639 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Ecological aspects==
The plant grows on the muddy margins of ponds where it forms carpets with 100% cover, semi-submerged in deeper water, or totally submerged with elongated stems. It does not die back in winter.<ref name="hackney" /> It has been reported to be very tolerant to copper toxicity<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Küpper|first1=Hendrik|last2=Küpper|first2=Frithjof|last3=Spiller|first3=Martin|date=1996|title=Environmental relevance of heavy metal-substituted chlorophylls using the example of water plants|journal=Journal of Experimental Botany|volume=47|issue=2|pages=259–266|doi=10.1093/jxb/47.2.259|issn=0022-0957|doi-access=free}}</ref> and to be a [[hyperaccumulator]] of copper.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Küpper|first1=Hendrik|last2=Götz|first2=Birgit|last3=Mijovilovich|first3=Ana|last4=Küpper|first4=Frithjof C.|last5=Meyer-Klaucke|first5=Wolfram|date=2009-10-01|title=Complexation and Toxicity of Copper in Higher Plants. I. Characterization of Copper Accumulation, Speciation, and Toxicity in Crassula helmsii as a New Copper Accumulator|url=http://www.plantphysiol.org/content/151/2/702|journal=Plant Physiology|language=en|volume=151|issue=2|pages=702–714|doi=10.1104/pp.109.139717|issn=0032-0889|pmc=2754650|pmid=19641032}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''C. helmsii'' is able to grow fully submerged in a cool-water [[aquarium]] or as a submersed or marginal plant in a [[pond]]. Once established it can grow vigorously and may need to be trimmed back. Schedule 9 of the UK [[Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981]] lists this plant as one that must not be caused to grow in the wild.<ref name="uksi">{{UK SI
